nodes.name: Gold microelectrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: 16mm×16mm SiO2 (285 nm)/Si chips with a prepatterned set of 32 Au contact pads were fabricated via conventional photolithography. Colloidal PMMA solution was dropped onto the chip and spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 1 min and then baked at 100°C for 5 min. Disc patterns for gold disc microelectrodes with radius from 2 to 50 μm and contact electrode patterns were opened by electron-beam lithography (TECAN VEGA) at a dosage of 210 μC cm⁻². After the deposition of Au (60 nm) by thermal evaporation (NANO 36, Kurt. J. Lesker), the chip was immersed in acetone to remove the PMMA resist and rinsed with acetone, isopropanol and pure water. After drying the chip with N₂, the device was spin-coated with PMMA at 1200 rpm for 1 min (with a thickness of 1000 nm) and baked at 150°C for 10 min. The process was repeated once to obtain a PMMA thickness of 2 μm, and remove residual solvent and pinholes. Then, gold disc microelectrodes were exposed by EBL, and the recessed microelectrodes with PMMA channels were formed.

nodes.name: Pristine 2H-MoS2 OCEM fabrication
nodes.procedure: 2H-MoS2 nanosheets were obtained by mechanical exfoliation of 2H-MoS2 crystal (2D Semiconductors) and deposited on the SiO2 (285 nm)/Si chip prepatterned with Au contact pads. The chip bearing the MoS2 nanosheet was spin-coated with PMMA and baked at 140 °C for 5 min. Standard EBL was used to define the two-terminal contact on MoS2 nanosheet at a dosage of 210 μC cm⁻². Thermal evaporation was used to deposit the Cr (8 nm)/Au (32 nm) contacts on the MoS2 nanosheet and contact with the Au contact pads, followed by the lift-off process in acetone. Then the circular reaction windows were fabricated following the same procedures as in fabricating the recessed gold microelectrode above.

nodes.name: Ar-plasma treatment of MoS2
nodes.procedure: Plasma treatment of 2H MoS2 nanosheet was performed in Ion 40 Plasma System (PVA Tepla America, Inc.), equipped with 13.56 MHz generator operating at 100 W. Plasma parameters (plasma power of 100 W, gas pressure of 1.2 mbar, and predefined exposure time) were selected to achieve desired properties, as shown in the results. The OCEM based on 2H MoS2 was loaded on a transfer plate and inserted into the plasma chamber; initially, the chamber was completely evacuated to 0.010 mbar and then filled with argon (Ar 99.999%) up to a pressure of 1.2 mbar. The plasma was generated at 100 W and maintained for the desired period (0-10 min).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of MoS2 show characteristic E₂g¹ peak at ~384 cm⁻¹ and A₁g peak at ~409 cm⁻¹ with blue shifts after Ar-plasma treatment; peak intensities drop with increasing plasma duration indicating crystal disorders.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For pristine MoS2, the characteristic Raman peaks are E₂g¹ (about 384 cm⁻¹) and A₁g (about 409 cm⁻¹) active modes. As shown in Figure 4b, the Ar-plasma treatment resulted in a blue shift of both A₁g mode and E₂g¹ mode...

nodes.characterization_summary: PL peak of MoS2 shows blueshift after 10-min Ar-plasma treatment due to band filling effect from p-doping by oxygen adsorption on defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the PL peak shows blueshift after 10-min Ar-plasma treatment, which likely resulted from the band filling effect.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ids-Vds measurements show conductance of MoS2 decreases with Ar-plasma treatment duration, dropping over two orders of magnitude after 10 min due to increased surface defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4d, the plasma treatment results in a clear decrease in the conductance of MoS2, likely resulting from the increased surface defects.
